nysmm_phisterer_sketch.organization: Fonda, NY; mustered in Oct 17-18 1862, three years; Cols. William T. Miller / Duncan McMartin. Seven companies organized at Fonda, three at Plattsburgh.
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.recruitment_counties: Fulton, Montgomery, Saratoga, Clinton, Essex, Warren.
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.company_I_locale_verbatim: Company I: 'Champlain, Chesterfield, Plattsburg and AuSable' (Clinton County) — matches Charles F. Hubbell enlisting at Champlain.
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.corps: Defenses of Washington (Oct 1862); 22nd Corps (Feb 1863); Department of the Gulf, 19th (XIX) Corps, 1st Brigade, 1st (Emory's) Division (Feb 1864); Army of the Shenandoah (Mar 1865).
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.campaigns_verbatim: Red River Campaign (LA): Sabine Cross Roads/Mansfield Apr 8, Pleasant Hill ('severe loss'), Mansura. Sheridan's Shenandoah Valley: Opequon/Third Winchester Sep 19 1864 ('69 killed and wounded'), Fisher's Hill, Strasburg, Cedar Creek Oct 19 1864 ('81 killed, wounded and missing'); then Savannah/Georgia.
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.losses_verbatim: 202 total deaths (1 officer + 40 men killed/died of wounds; 1 officer + 160 men of disease).
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.significance_for_charles: The regiment lost FOUR TIMES as many men to DISEASE (161) as to combat (41) — the context in which Charles contracted the illness that killed him in 1875.
nysmm_phisterer_sketch.claude_reasoning: C4: Co. I = Champlain/Clinton Co. corroborates the hometown lock. C3: the XIX Corps campaign arc (Red River -> Shenandoah) situates Charles's and James's service and the Cedar Creek wound.
